questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was a place where English was spoken.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay, most information were on the website and we had a meeting with a coordinator in Bath who finalized the last things like courses.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: You were assigned a contact person who registered you for the courses you had selected beforehand.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. You were given a link to a website, though with limited options.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Choose a place close to the city center.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Nice place, but very expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were issues regarding credit transfer on the part of KU, but otherwise it was fine, as the contact person handled everything.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Your contact person sends an email a few months before you are due to leave, asking you to select the subjects you would like to take. I couldn't see which courses were available, so I had to email them to request a course catalogue. Upon arrival in Bath, you meet with your contact person to confirm your chosen courses and/or select new ones.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: you were given a contact person in Bath who is there to help you.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got both of the courses I chose.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pay attention to the exam format and consider which type of exam you prefer. Some courses do not have a final exam but instead involve assignments submitted throughout the semester, presentations, or a combination of these. I wish I had given this more thought when choosing my courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I thought both of my courses were good.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It consists only of lectures. The syllabus relies heavily on scientific articles.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Bachelor projekt, Global health and Drug Targets in the Immune System.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend both. Global Health was a relaxed course with an oral presentation at the end, while Drug Targets in the Immune System was exciting but a bit more challenging academically.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Rent was by far the biggest expense; otherwise, prices were very similar to those back home in Denmark.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It was very similar to the prices back home in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of clubs are available at the university. Sports, creative, and cultural.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of them. The more you sign up for, the more people you meet. It’s also very relaxed, so you aren’t obliged to attend every single time.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See other parts of England and explore as much of the area as possible. Places in England I would recommend include the Cotswolds, the Lake District, and the Seven Sisters hike, a long hike near Brighton. There are good transport options from Bath to the major cities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: There was not that big of a culture shock.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs and don't be afraid to approach people on your course and talk to them. Most people are very friendly and open to meeting new people. Also the clubs have a lot of socials outside of school that makes it easier to meet local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Do not think there were any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Going to the pub and hanging out with friends.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open, say yes to everything, and just dive right in.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sorting out the courses before leaving was a bit of a hassle. If you’re going with someone else from KU, definitely talk to them about it and help each other out. Also, I would choose courses that don’t have a final exam at the end (if possible), as the studying became very intense during the exam period, though that really depends on your personal preference.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting lots of lovely people and having experiences you’ll remember for the rest of your life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting approval sorted out for the courses was definitely a challenge. Communication from both KU and the host university was often poor, you frequently had to call or email them multiple times just to get an answer.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
